trigger: a policy element with a near-1MB identifier and thousands of short parameters stays under kMaxRows while re-embedding that near-1MB identifier into every one of those rows
summary: The adversarial-review round's row cap (kMaxRows) bounds row COUNT but not row BYTES -- an item's identifier is re-embedded into every row it produces, so a pathological identifier could amplify to hundreds of MB before the row-count cap engages, worse than the adversarial review's own 100MB probe. Fixed: added a 256-byte cap on the identifier before it becomes a row's source field (kMaxSourceIdentifierBytes), closing the amplification vector directly. Regression test proves a huge identifier never reaches the wire untruncated.
